_meta.purpose: A SHARED PUBLIC REGISTRY of pinned PGS models: trait → PGS identifier. There are nobody's genotypes here — only the public IDs of PGS Catalog models.
_meta.why: A percentile has meaning only inside a specific model: each has its own set of variants, training sample and reference distribution. The just-prs server ranking changes over time, and without pinning one and the same genome receives different percentiles from run to run (up to ±68 percentiles was observed on traits with a weak genetic architecture). That is why the model of a trait is pinned here and is changed only deliberately.
_meta.policy: The life cycle of a model: (1) percentiles are computed only with the pinned model; (2) a run where the server preferred another one does NOT change the values — the model that did not match is recorded as a candidate with a dossier (when it was noticed, how many runs in a row, quality, coverage, whether there is a reference percentile; personal percentiles are not written into the registry); (3) prs_model_review.py gives recommendations once a quarter: REJECT without a reference percentile or with coverage <0.95; MAY BE ACCEPTED when the quality is above that of the pinned one or when it is stable over ≥2 runs with quality not lower; otherwise WAIT; (4) acceptance is pointwise, prs_results_build.py --accept-model <trait>: the old model goes into history, a mark about the break of the series stays in the profile — percentiles before and after the change are not comparable. A shift of the percentile is never a ground on its own.

reference_population.method: ancestry_check.py: the log-likelihood of 317 genotypes from the BAM under the 1000G phase 3 frequencies (Ensembl)
reference_population.evidence: the EUR posterior ≈ 1.0; ΔLL to the nearest one (AMR, itself half European by origin) = 22.2 ≈ a likelihood ratio of 4×10⁹
reference_population.sensitivity: the sensitivity of the percentiles to the choice of reference has been measured (profile/prs_ancestry_sensitivity.json): the median spread between populations is 26.7 pp, in 29/69 models it is ≥30 pp — the choice of reference matters, and it has been confirmed
reference_population.policy: compute the percentiles against EUR; pgsc_calc --run_ancestry is not required until the ancestry is called into question (e.g. another user of the package — run ancestry_check.py again)
